When companies in the same industry propose merging with one another, they often claim that the merger will benefit consumers by increasing efficiency and therefore lowering prices. Economist Ying Fan investigated this notion in the context of the United States newspaper market. She modeled a hypothetical merger of Minneapolis-area newspapers and found that subscription prices would rise following a merger.
Text 2
Economists Dario Focarelli and Fabio Panetta have argued that research on the effect of mergers on prices has focused excessively on short-term effects, which tend to be adverse for consumers. Using the case of consumer banking in Italy, they show that over the long term (several years, in their study), the efficiency gains realized by merged companies do result in economic benefits for consumers.
o9.stem: Based on the texts, how would Focarelli and Panetta (Text 2) most likely respond to Fan’s findings (Text 1)?

opts.B: They would argue that over the long term the expenses incurred by the merged newspaper company will also increase.
opts.C: They would encourage Fan to investigate whether the projected effect on subscription prices persists over an extended period.
opts.D: They would claim that mergers have a different effect on consumer prices in the newspaper industry than in most other industries.

[Graph: Percentage of Nonhexagonal Cells (5-sided, 7-sided, and 8-sided) in Hives of Three Honeybee Species]

Notes: A records office classifies documents by risk; documents whose release could cause minor harm are Restricted; documents whose release could cause major harm are Sealed; routine budget drafts could cause minor but not major harm; the goal is to classify the drafts.
33.1.stem: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

opts.A: Because their release could cause minor but not major harm, routine budget drafts are classified as Restricted.
opts.B: Sealed documents could cause major harm if released.
opts.C: The records office classifies documents by release risk.
opts.D: Budget drafts are one kind of government document.

33.2.body: In a university archive, scholars examined correspondence, field notes, and early drafts that revealed how a project changed over time. The materials did not overturn the basic history of the project, but they clarified the roles of several participants and made one previously simple interpretation seem less adequate. Notes: A lab labels materials by hazard; materials that can irritate skin are Caution; materials that can cause severe injury are Danger; diluted cleaner can irritate skin but cannot cause severe injury; the goal is to classify diluted cleaner.
33.2.stem: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

opts.A: Danger materials can cause severe injury.
opts.B: Diluted cleaner is handled in a lab.
opts.C: The lab uses hazard categories for materials.
opts.D: Since it can irritate skin but cannot cause severe injury, diluted cleaner is labeled Caution.

33.3.body: A museum catalog presents an artist, object, or performance in relation to the social and technical conditions that shaped it. Instead of merely naming the work, the catalog connects materials, audience, historical moment, and purpose so readers can understand why a particular description or conclusion is warranted. Notes: A library classifies manuscripts by fragility; items that need careful handling are Monitored; items that cannot be handled by readers are Restricted; most nineteenth-century pamphlets need careful handling but can still be handled; the goal is to classify the pamphlets.
33.3.stem: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

opts.A: Restricted manuscripts cannot be handled by readers.
opts.B: Most nineteenth-century pamphlets are classified as Monitored because they need careful handling but can still be handled by readers.
opts.C: The library classifies manuscripts by fragility.

33.4.body: A public-policy study compares outcomes across several communities that adopted similar measures under different local conditions. Because the evidence includes exceptions as well as broad patterns, the researchers choose cautious wording and distinguish between what the data directly show and what they merely suggest. Notes: An agency classifies storms by expected impact; storms expected to cause local disruption are Advisory; storms expected to cause widespread damage are Emergency; a coastal storm is expected to cause local disruption but not widespread damage; the goal is to classify the storm.
33.4.stem: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

opts.C: The agency classifies storms by expected impact.
opts.D: Expected to cause local disruption but not widespread damage, the coastal storm is classified as Advisory.

33.5.body: In a scientific investigation, the outcome depends on a sequence of observations rather than on one dramatic discovery. The researchers describe the method, the comparison group, and the limits of the evidence before drawing a conclusion that must be stated with both precision and restraint. Notes: A museum classifies loans by security risk; objects that could be damaged by ordinary handling are Supervised; objects that could be seriously damaged by brief exposure are Restricted; most ceramic replicas could be damaged by ordinary handling but not seriously damaged by brief exposure; the goal is to classify the replicas.
33.5.stem: Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

opts.A: Ceramic replicas may be used in educational displays.
opts.B: Restricted objects could be seriously damaged by brief exposure.
opts.C: Most ceramic replicas are classified as Supervised because ordinary handling could damage them.
opts.D: Museum loans are classified by security risk.
